business_problem: Telefónica needs to evolve and maintain a very large API and microservices estate without slowing delivery, while keeping integrations understandable, compliant, secure and maintainable; it also wants to reduce manual effort in recurring internal IT support processes.
solution_summary: Telefónica describes an internal AI-enabled integration approach rather than a vendor product deployment. In development and integration work, generative AI is used as an accelerator around microservice delivery: it helps engineers understand unfamiliar systems, turns technical documentation into assistants that can answer API-field and response-format questions, and supports system mocking so integration tests can run with realistic service behaviour before full infrastructure is deployed. Telefónica also describes AI agents as the next layer of automation, with the ability to use the terminal, install dependencies, run scripts, inspect error messages and resolve issues across end-to-end workflows. In operations, the company has integrated an AI agent into IT support so some onboarding-related access requests can be answered automatically. The source does not name model providers, storage platforms or serving infrastructure, but it does emphasize private infrastructure, least-privilege access, and guardrails for deterministic, validated use in critical systems.

solution_components.name: generative AI
solution_components.role: Used to accelerate microservice development, interpret technical documentation, answer API questions and simulate service behaviour for integration testing.

solution_components.name: AI agent
solution_components.role: Automates end-to-end workflows such as running terminal tasks and responding to some internal IT support access requests.

data_flow: Technical documentation, API definitions and support requests are provided to generative AI and AI agents; the AI interprets documentation, simulates service responses for testing, or handles workflow steps such as answering access tickets, and the outputs are consumed by developers, integrators and internal support users.
business_outcome: Telefónica reports faster software delivery, more accessible system knowledge for integration teams, automated handling of some recurring IT support tasks, and a move toward more efficient, secure and scalable digital integration.
architecture_clues: Telefónica says it uses private infrastructure and strict agreements to protect confidential data.
The company says agents should operate under the principle of least privilege.
Guardrails are required so AI responses in critical systems meet deterministic standards.
Generative AI is used for system mocking to support integration tests before full infrastructure deployment.
